name: commercetools
title: commercetools SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce
description: Svelte Commerce on commercetools: 21 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in through the /me endpoints. Setup, environment, limits and fixes.
lede: The commercetools connector models version-based optimistic concurrency — `{ version, actions: [] }` — throughout, and is wired against the `/me` endpoints so nothing runs unscoped. Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired, all through the `/me` endpoints; countries, currencies, CMS pages and vendors are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your commercetools project

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_URL
env.note: The project-scoped root, `https://api.{region}.commercetools.com/{projectKey}`. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_KEY
env.note: The API client’s `client_id`, sent as HTTP Basic to the auth host only.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_SECRET
env.note: The API client’s `client_secret`. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as a bearer token when set.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_STORE_ID
env.note: A Store key: requests go through `/in-store/key={storeKey}`.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_CHANNEL_ID
env.note: A Channel ID, sent as a reference in request bodies and as the price channel on reads — not as a path segment.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_REGION
env.note: Such as `europe-west1.gcp`. Needed only when it cannot be read from the API URL.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_PROJECT_KEY
env.note: Defaults to the last path segment of the API URL.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_AUTH_URL
env.note: OAuth host override. Defaults to the API host with `api.` replaced by `auth.`.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_SCOPE
env.note: Space-separated OAuth scopes requested when a token is issued.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_LOCALE
env.note: Used to flatten localised strings and build `where` and `sort` predicates. Defaults to `en`.

env.name: PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_CURRENCY
env.note: ISO 4217 currency for cart and price selection.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/commercetools-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_*` variable that is set, camel-cased: `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_PROJECT_KEY` arrives as `projectKey`. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_ACCESS_KEY`; the connector’s source does not read it.
backendSettings: Create an API client for the storefront with only the scopes a shopper’s session needs: its ID and secret reach the browser.
howItWorks: commercetools updates a resource by sending its current `version` and a list of `actions`; the connector models that throughout, so a stale write fails rather than overwrites. It works through the `/me` endpoints, scoped to the signed-in or anonymous shopper, so no call returns another customer’s data. Tokens come from the auth host, with the API client’s ID and secret as HTTP Basic.
limitations: The API client’s ID and secret come from `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_SECRET`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor can read them; the client’s scopes are what limit the damage.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the commercetools connector is active but PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/commercetools-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: `[commercetools] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if commercetools has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

faq.q: Can I run a commercetools project on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired through the `/me` endpoints; countries, currencies, CMS pages and vendors are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production commercetools project.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to commercetools?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/commercetools-connector`, set `PUBLIC_COMMERCETOOLS_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Does the connector use the /me endpoints or the Checkout API?
faq.a: The `/me` endpoints, with an anonymous token for guests, so nothing runs unscoped. The Svelte Commerce maintainers have asked commercetools whether that is the idiomatic pattern for a headless storefront, or whether the Checkout and Frontend APIs are.

openQuestion: For a headless storefront, is the `/me` surface plus an anonymous token the idiomatic pattern, or should the connector use the Checkout or Frontend APIs instead?

api.surface: The connector calls the commercetools Composable Commerce HTTP API, a JSON REST API whose paths are relative to the project-scoped root `https://api.{region}.commercetools.com/{projectKey}`, with tokens requested from a second host, `https://auth.{region}.commercetools.com`.
api.auth: Every API call carries `Authorization: Bearer`; a guest gets an anonymous-session token from `/oauth/{projectKey}/anonymous/token` with an `anonymous_id` the connector generates, a shopper who signs in gets a password-flow token from `/oauth/{projectKey}/customers/token`, and the token, refresh token and scope are kept in `localStorage` under `ct_session` so a reload keeps the same identity; logout is local only, because commercetools has no revocation endpoint.

calls.what: `GET /product-projections` with `limit`, `offset`, `sort`, `priceCurrency` and `storeProjection`; `GET /product-projections/key={key}` and `/product-projections/{id}`; `GET /product-projections/search` with `text.{locale}` and `fuzzy=true` for a text query
`GET /categories` with `where=slug(en="...")`, falling back to `GET /categories/key={key}` and `/categories/{id}`; the whole tree with `limit=500`
`GET /product-projections/search` with `filter.query=categories.id:subtree("{id}")`, a `variants.price.centAmount:range (...)` filter in minor units, and `facet=categories.id`

`GET /me/active-cart`, `POST /me/carts` to create, `GET /me/carts/{id}`, and `POST /me/carts/{id}` with `{ version, actions }`, each with `expand=discountCodes[*].discountCode` and `paymentInfo.payments[*]`

`GET /shipping-methods/matching-cart?cartId=`, `POST /me/payments` with `amountPlanned` and `paymentMethodInfo.method`, an `addPayment` action on the cart, then `POST /me/orders` with `{ id, version }`

rules: When an update returns 409 `ConcurrentModification`, the connector reads `currentVersion` from the error, or fetches the resource once, and replays the same actions exactly once; a second conflict goes back to the caller.
Localised fields cannot be compared directly, so the connector writes predicates as `slug(en="x")` and sorts as `name.en asc`, since `where=slug="x"` is a 400.

Page requests are clamped to the platform limits of 500 for `limit` and 10,000 for `offset`, totals are read from the body’s `{ limit, offset, count, total, results }`, and the page count is capped at what an offset of 10,000 can reach.

`GET /me/active-cart` answers 404 for a shopper with no cart, which the connector treats as an empty cart rather than an error; at sign-in it calls `/me/login` while still holding the anonymous token so the guest cart is merged rather than orphaned.

`GET /payment-methods` returns every PaymentMethod in the project, including other customers’ saved instruments, so the connector always adds a `where` predicate that keeps only methods with no customer attached, plus the signed-in customer’s own (`customer is not defined or customer(id=...)`).
